## How it works

- [statement] Negation finding: the optimal-range paper assumes flat, constant gas fees and continuously adjusted positions; it says continuous trading requires large initial wealth to overcome gas fees. Its proposed discrete alternative is to adjust when drift or fee profitability changes substantially, so its analytic optimum is not a ready-made rebalance cadence for a small bot. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2309.08431v3 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Revert Auto-Range documents a percentage-out-of-range trigger followed by withdrawal and recreation at the same width centered on current price. Its fee-source documentation also says inadequate gas budget can prevent triggering; the feature description is not a guarantee of uninterrupted range activity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.revert.finance/revert/auto-range · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Krystal documents independent lower/upper trigger prices, a time buffer requiring price to remain outside the trigger band, and a separately configured destination range. Its gas-fee ceiling can defer a rebalance. These controls illustrate that the trigger band, dwell time and new range are separate choices. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.krystal.app/products/liquidity-management/lp-management/lp-transactions/auto-rebalance · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Steer documents distinct trigger families: distance from range center, inactive range, percentage drift relative to range, directional range exit, and no automatic price trigger. It explicitly cautions that more frequent rebalancing raises gas costs and that triggers should reflect expected pair volatility. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.steer.finance/flagship-apps/smart-pools/Strategies/rebalance-triggers/ · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Fees alone do not establish LP profitability. The LVR paper separates market-risk exposure from a microstructural component of fees minus arbitrage losses, while the optimal-range paper balances fees against predictable loss, concentration risk and rebalancing costs. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06046 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.08431v3
- [statement] Charm describes a multi-position Alpha Vault strategy: full-range liquidity, a concentrated base order and a limit order. Managers choose concentration and out-of-range depth through parameters; this is a different strategy family from repeatedly moving one fixed-width band. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://learn.charm.fi/charm/manage-liquidity/how-it-works · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Narrower ranges concentrate fee earning while active but increase concentration risk and exposure to volatility-related loss. Cartea, Drissi and Monga derive an incentive to widen ranges as volatility increases; Gamma also describes narrow positions as more short volatility. This is a conditional tradeoff, not a universal optimal width. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2309.08431v3 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy · also: https://gammastrategies.medium.com/gamma-strategies-officially-launches-on-arbitrum-6416dad4b410
- [statement] In the Cartea–Drissi–Monga model, optimal range width depends on fees after gas, predictable loss and concentration risk. The strategy optimizes expected utility of terminal wealth rather than fee income alone. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2309.08431v3 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] The optimal-control paper allows a predictive drift signal to skew the range rather than always centering it symmetrically. That result is model-dependent and requires a signal; it does not establish a profitable directional forecast for Base pools. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2309.08431v3 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Impermanent loss and loss-versus-rebalancing compare against different benchmarks: holding the initial assets versus an idealized portfolio that follows AMM holdings through frictionless external trading. The term rebalancing in LVR does not mean a bot moving a concentrated-liquidity range. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23404v1 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Concentrated liquidity allocates capital to a chosen price interval. A position stops earning trading fees outside that interval; leaving the interval is an earning-state change, not itself an instruction to rebalance. (medium confidence) — https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/get-started/concepts/liquidity-providers/concentrated-liquidity · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.08431v3
- [statement] An out-of-range position can become active again without recentering if price returns. Uniswap describes the position becoming entirely one asset at the boundary; a bot must treat waiting and changing its range as distinct strategy choices. (low confidence) — https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/get-started/concepts/liquidity-providers/concentrated-liquidity · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Negation finding: Willetts and Harrington argue that frictionless LVR is an imperfect measure for comparing execution venues and propose RVR with centralized rebalancing frictions. Their paper focuses on fixed-weight and dynamic-weight AMMs, so it does not demonstrate that a Slipstream range-recentering bot is profitable. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23404v1 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Aero describes Slipstream rewards as restricted to liquidity in the active range and says out-of-range single-sided deposits can express a directional range-order view. Strategy design must distinguish active earning from intentionally resting outside the market. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://aero.xyz/llms-full.txt · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] Arrakis Pro describes treasury-owned liquidity for token issuers. Its Flagship strategy concentrates around spot and adapts to volatility; its market-making system monitors price, volatility and inventory to choose rebalances. These are issuer inventory objectives, which should not be assumed identical to a personal LP bot objective. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.arrakis.finance/text/introduction/arrakisPro.html · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
- [statement] In its historical Arbitrum launch description, Gamma distinguishes market-price reset bounds for dynamic wide/narrow ranges from NAV-based reset bounds for pegged-price assets. The latter may deliberately remain out of range while market price deviates from NAV; this is historical strategy evidence, not verification of present Base or Slipstream support. (low confidence) — https://gammastrategies.medium.com/gamma-strategies-officially-launches-on-arbitrum-6416dad4b410 · keywords: Concentrated-liquidity range management and rebalancing strategy
